answers.core: It seems like a functionality that complements SceneTree's `call_group()` - using groups as an abstraction layer towards interacting with individual nodes.
answers.workaround:
Workarounds are feasible, but inelegant:
* Implement listener-dependent code in nodes that emit the signals (against best practices)
* Pass around references to the listener to every entity that might instantiate an emitter
* React to SceneTree's `node_added`, check whether the node is part of a group, if yes connect it. This does not work if the node is added to the group after its creation (see #627, #1259).
* Continuously check for nodes within a group and connect them as soon as they show up (terrible for performance)

title: Add a `group_connect()` method to monitor signals from any nodes within a group
